title: A look at FrogPop, the first game I'm making with AI tools
author: PerspectivePersonal
selftext:
I'm making FrogPop, a Unity roguelite inspired by Bubble Trouble. You play as a frog, pop bouncing bubbles with your tongue, and pick up bugs and relics that change your attacks.

I shared the beetle armor here last time. This clip gives a better idea of the rest of the game, including some powers and bosses.

Claude helped build the core game systems, and I use Codex for fixes and testing. Some art was made with PixelLab and OpenAI image generation, then edited and integrated. No generative AI runs during gameplay.

The recent serpent cleanup is a useful example of the work after generating an asset. The source sprites were already crisp, but the head, body and tail were being displayed at different scales. Reducing the whole character's resolution lost detail. Adjusting the existing rig's scale settings kept the artwork intact. The attacks and attachments still needed to be checked in Unity afterward.

There's a free browser demo of the first 10 waves: [https://blion247.itch.io/frogpop-demo](https://blion247.itch.io/frogpop-demo)

It's still an older build. The video combines separate development captures, and the full game will be paid: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5067810/FrogPop/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5067810/FrogPop/)
